summary.text: David Kustoff is a Memphis-area attorney and Republican who has represented Tennessee's 8th District since January 2017. Before Congress he led Shelby County's Republican Party, served as U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee, and sat on the Tennessee Higher Education Commission. He serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and is seeking re-election.

paragraphs.text: Kustoff was born and raised in Shelby County and attended White Station High School. He earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Memphis and graduated in 1992 from its Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law, then opened a law firm in Memphis that year, according to his official biography.

He chaired the Shelby County Republican Party from 1995 to 1999, and was Tennessee chairman of Lamar Alexander's 2002 U.S. Senate campaign and of the Bush/Cheney presidential campaigns in 2000 and 2004.

President George W. Bush appointed Kustoff U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee in 2006, and the Senate confirmed him. In that role he oversaw the majority of the Tennessee Waltz public-corruption trials, which sent 12 defendants, including Sen. John Ford, to federal prison.

He joined the board of BankTennessee in 2010. In 2015 Gov. Bill Haslam appointed him to the Tennessee Higher Education Commission, where he oversaw implementation of the Tennessee Promise last-dollar community-college scholarship program and Tennessee Reconnect.
Kustoff was elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024. He is in his fifth term and was unopposed in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary.
He serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and its Subcommittees on Tax and Health, and chairs the House-Knesset Parliamentary Friendship Group.
According to his official biography, Kustoff lives in Germantown with his wife, Roberta, and they have two children.
